title: Library System Schema Design
description: Model a library with books, authors, members, and loan records

data.text: Library systems track books, authors, copies, members, loans, and fines. The schema must support catalog browsing, availability checks, and loan history while enforcing business rules.

data.title: Library DDL
data.content: Design books, authors, copies, members, loans, and fines with availability tracking.

data.title: Tip
data.text: Use a book_authors junction table for many-to-many authorship. Avoid storing multiple author names in a single books column.

items.question: How do I track book editions?
items.answer: Add an edition table or include edition_number and published_year in books. Use ISBN when available.

items.question: How do I calculate overdue fines?
items.answer: Use a generated fines table populated by a scheduled job, or calculate on the fly with CASE expressions.

items.question: Should copies be individual rows?
items.answer: Yes. One copy per physical item enables accurate availability tracking and loan history per unit.

data.title: Summary
points: Separate book metadata from physical copies
Use a many-to-many table for authors
Track loan dates and return status explicitly
Store availability in book_copies for fast lookups
data.takeaway: Library schemas need physical inventory granularity and accurate loan state tracking to support both browsing and circulation operations.
